label: Line
_note: Promoted 2026-09-16 (verified_by sean). Every claim is a verbatim quote from the cited live Wikipedia article, verified by substring match. Selection rule is editorial (labelled).

citations.quote: Monofilament fishing line (shortened to just mono) is fishing line made from a single fiber of plastic material, as opposed to multifilament or braided fishing lines constructed from multiple strands of fibers.
Most fishing lines are now nylon monofilament because they are cheap to manufacture and can be produced in a range of diameters which have different tensile strengths
Fishermen often use monofilament because of its buoyant characteristics and its ability to stretch under load.
The line stretch has advantages, such as damping the force when setting the hook and when fighting strong fish.
Monofilament line is also available in different colors, such as clear, white, green, blue, red, and fluorescent.
Fluorocarbon fishing line is made of the fluoropolymer PVDF and it is valued for its refractive index, which is similar to that of water, making it less visible to fish.
It is denser than nylon, too, which makes it sink faster.
Because the elastic stretching is only a fraction of that of nylon monofilament, the contact with fish or bait is more direct.

Fluorocarbon lines have greater surface hardness than nylon lines and are more abrasion-resistant against underwater rocks and snags, yet are more shock-resilient than braided lines when fighting fish, thus making them ideal to use as leader lines

They also have less memory, stretch and moisture expansion than nylon lines, making it easier to keep the line taut and transmit vibrations, which is essential in lure fishing where the angler is very reliant on tactile sensitivity.

Braided line was one of the earliest types of fishing line, and in its modern incarnations it is still very popular in some situations because of its high knot strength, lack of stretch, and great overall power in relation to its diameter.
Braided lines often have 1/3 to 1/4 the diameter of mono or fluorocarbon lines at a given test breaking strength.
Braided lines have very little stretch, making fishing rigs very sensitive to fish bites; This is very important for both deep sea fishing and when targeting fish with a gentle bite.
Due to their flexibility, lack of stretch and most important, slippery surface, braided lines are hard to knot properly.
Due to the minimal stretch of braided line, hard-hitting fish will frequently cause the line to break.
Recently, other alternatives to standard nylon monofilament lines have been introduced made of copolymers or fluorocarbon, or a combination of the two materials.

Most copolymer lines are nylon-based polymer blends fusing a blend of nylon with another higher-density one, although recently "tripolymer" lines that fuse three different blends of nylon have also appeared on the market.

notes.quote: Other factors relevant to certain fishing practices include breaking strength, knot strength, UV resistance, castability, limpness, stretch, memory, abrasion resistance, and visibility.

recommend._note: Editorial pick→line rule, grounded in each type's CITED properties (quoted above); the rule itself is not a sourced fact. Per-entry overrides beat the style fallback.

why.fluorocarbon: sinks, is less visible (refractive index near water), and has less stretch/memory for direct contact
why.monofilament: buoyant and stretches under load, which damps the surge on a hooked fish
why.braid: small diameter, lack of stretch, and high strength-to-diameter for cover and solid hooksets
why.copolymer: a nylon-based blend — between mono and fluoro
